We have mass spec m/z 276.0666 (M+? likely molecular ion). That corresponds to formula C14H12O6 (calc mass: C14=168, H12=12, O6=96 => total 276). So matches. Need SMILES. We have many candidate isomers from isomer list. Need to match NMR data.

Proton NMR: signals: 1.29 t (3H) and 4.30 q (2H) typical ethyl ester (CH3-CH2-O). So ethoxy group present. Also aromatic region: 7.29 dd (4H), 7.75 dd (1H), 7.98 ddd (2H). That's total aromatic protons: 4+1+2 =7? Wait 4+1+2 =7. But total protons: 3+2+7 =12 matches formula H12. So aromatic system with 7 aromatic H suggests a benzene ring with substitution pattern giving 7 H? But benzene has max 5 substituents; 7 aromatic H suggests two aromatic rings? Let's think: total aromatic protons 7 suggests maybe a naphthalene? Naphthalene has 8 H. But 7 suggests one substitution on naphthalene (monosubstituted) gives 7 H. So likely a naphthalene core with ethoxy carbonyl etc.

Carbon NMR: peaks: 166.00, 151.10, 144.35, 140.45, 137.05, 131.30 (x2), 124.40, 122.30, 119.00, 116.65 (x2), 61.10, 14.26.

166 ppm likely carbonyl of ester (C=O). 151-144 aromatic carbons attached to O maybe. 61.10 is O-CH2 of ethoxy, 14.26 is CH3.

We need a structure with ethyl ester attached to aromatic system, plus maybe another carbonyl (maybe carboxylic acid). The formula has 6 oxygens: ethoxy carbonyl (2 O), plus maybe two more carbonyls (e.g., dicarboxylic acid) and maybe phenoxy? Let's examine candidate SMILES that include ethoxy group: "CCOC(=O)CC#CC1=C(C=CC(=C1)C(=O)O)C(=O)O" includes ethoxy carbonyl attached to propargyl chain, not aromatic protons pattern (has alkyne). Not match.

Another candidate with ethoxy: "CCOC(=O)CC#CC1=..." not.

Look at list: "C1OC2=C(C=CC(=C2OC1)/C=C/C(=O)O)/C=C/C(=O)O" has ethoxy? No.

"CC1=CC(=CC2=C1C(=O)C=C(O2)C(=O)O)O" no ethoxy.

"CC1=CC2([C@@H]3[C@H](C1[C@H]4[C@@H]2C(=O)OC4=O)C(=O)OC3=O)C" complex.

We need ethoxy group: pattern "CCO" at start. Candidates with "CCO": first one "C1=CC=C(C=C1)COCOC2=COC(=CC2=O)C(=O)O" has "COCOC" not ethoxy.

Second "CC(=C)C(=O)OC1CC2=C1C=CC(=C2C(=O)O)C(=O)O" has "OC1" not ethoxy.

Third "CC1=CC(=CC2=C1C(=O)C=C(O2)CC(=O)CC(=O)O)O" has "CC1" but not ethoxy.

Fourth "CC1=CC2([C@@H]3..." no.

Fifth "CC1=CC(=CC(=C1)OC2=CC(=C(C(=C2)O)O)C(=O)O)O" has "CC1" but not ethoxy.

Sixth "C1=CC=C(C=C1)OC(=O)O.C1=CC=C(C(=C1)C(=O)O)O" mixture.

Seventh "C1OC2=C(C=CC(=C2OC1)/C=C/C(=O)O)/C=C/C(=O)O" no ethoxy.

Eighth "C1=CC2=C(C=C(C=C2)OCC(=O)O)C(=C1)OCC(=O)O" has "OCC(=O)O" ethoxy? That's O-CH2-COOH not ethoxy.

Ninth "CC(=O)O[C@@H]1[C@H](C(=O)C2=CC=CC=C2C1=O)OC(=O)C" no ethoxy.

Tenth "CC(=O)C1=C(C=C(C2=C1OC=C(C2=O)C=O)OC)OC" no ethoxy.

Eleventh "CCCC(=O)OC1=CC=CC2=C1C(=O)C=C(O2)C(=O)O" has "CCCC(=O)O" but not ethoxy.

Twelfth "CCOC(=O)CC#CC1=C(C=CC(=C1)C(=O)O)C(=O)O" we already looked.

Thirteenth "C1=CC2=C(C=CC(=C2O)CC(=O)O)C(=C1CC(=O)O)O" no ethoxy.

Fourteenth "C1=CC2=C(C=CC(=C2)C(=O)O)C=C1C(C(C(=O)O)O)O" no ethoxy.

Fifteenth "CC1=C(C2=CC(=C(C=C2O1)C(=O)C)OC(=O)C)C(=O)O" has "CC1=" but not ethoxy.

Sixteenth "C1C(C(=O)OC1=O)C2=CC=C(C=C2)C(CC=O)C(=O)O" no ethoxy.

Seventeenth "C1=CC(=CC=C1CC(=O)O)OCC2=CC=C(O2)C(=O)O" has "OCC" but not ethoxy.

Thus only candidate with ethoxy group is the one we tested (CCOC...). That matches ethoxy signals. So likely correct structure: ethyl 2-(naphthalene-1,5-dicarboxylic acid?) Wait structure: CCOC(=O)CC#CC1=... includes alkyne, not aromatic protons pattern.

But our proton NMR shows only aromatic protons, no alkyne. So maybe ethoxy attached to carbonyl directly attached to aromatic ring (ethyl benzoate). Ethyl benzoate would have aromatic 5 H, not 7. So need additional aromatic ring.

Maybe ethyl 2-(naphthalen-1-yl)acetate? That would have ethoxy and aromatic 7 H (naphthalene mono-substituted). Formula C14H12O2? Actually ethyl naphthalene-1-carboxylate: C13H12O2? Wait naphthalene (C10H8) + CO2Et (C3H5O2) = C13H13O2? Not match.

Our formula has 6 O, many carbonyls. Ethoxy carbonyl plus two more carbonyls (maybe two carboxylic acids). So maybe ethyl 2,6-dihydroxy-naphthalene-1,4-dicarboxylate? But O count high.

Let's compute: Ethyl ester adds C2H5O (plus carbonyl O). That's C2H5O2? Actually ethyl carboxylate: -COOCH2CH3 adds C3H5O2 (C=O OCH2CH3). So 3 C, 5 H, 2 O.

Remaining formula after subtracting ethyl ester: total C14H12O6 minus C3H5O2 = C11H7O4. Need aromatic system with 11 C, 7 H, 4 O (likely two carboxylic acids). Naphthalene core C10H6, plus one extra carbon (maybe carbonyl carbon) gives C11H6? plus OH? Hmm.

If we have naphthalene-1,5-dicarboxylic acid (C12H8O4). Add ethyl ester on one acid gives C15H12O5? Not.

Let's think of structure: Ethyl 2,6-dihydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone? That has many O.

But carbon NMR shows one carbonyl at 166 ppm (ester). Others aromatic carbons 151-119. No carbonyl around 200 ppm (ketone). So only one carbonyl? But formula has 6 O, so other O are phenolic OH or ether.

166 ppm could be ester carbonyl. No other carbonyl signals (like 170-180 for acid). So maybe the other O are phenolic OH (no carbonyl). So we have ethyl ester plus 4 phenolic OH groups? That would be C14H12O6 (6 O). Ethyl ester contributes 2 O, leaving 4 OH. Aromatic protons 7 suggests phenolic substitution pattern: naphthalene with 4 OH and one ethoxy carbonyl substituent. That would reduce aromatic H count: naphthalene has 8 H; each OH replaces H, each ethoxy carbonyl replaces H. So 8 - (4 OH) - (1 ester) = 3 aromatic H, not 7. So not.

Maybe a benzene ring with 2 carbonyl groups (ester and acid) and ethoxy, plus other O as phenoxy? Let's examine carbon NMR: many downfield aromatic carbons (151-144) likely attached to O (phenoxy). So multiple phenoxy groups.

The proton NMR aromatic pattern: 4H doublet of doublets at 7.29 (dd, J 8.7,1.7) suggests ortho-coupled protons in a para-disubstituted phenyl? 4H could be two equivalent phenyl rings each with 2 H? But 4H dd suggests maybe two overlapping signals.

7.75 dd (1H) and 7.98 ddd (2H) total 3 H. So aromatic total 7 H, could be a phenyl ring with 4 H (para-disubstituted) plus a monosubstituted phenyl (5 H) but we have only 3 extra. Not.

Maybe structure is ethyl 4-hydroxybenzoate with additional phenoxy groups? Hmm.

Let's use search tool to find similar SMILES with formula C14H12O6 and ethoxy group. Use search_by_smiles with generic? Could try to search for "CCOC(=O)" pattern. But we can also simulate spectra for candidate and compare.

We have candidate list; only one with ethoxy is the alkyne one, which likely not match. But maybe there are others with ethoxy not obvious: "CC1=CC(=CC2=C1C(=O)C=C(O2)CC(=O)CC(=O)O)O" includes "CC1=" but that's a methyl attached to aromatic, not ethoxy.

Thus maybe the ethoxy signals could be from ethoxy attached to carbonyl but not necessarily present; could be ethoxy from ethyl ester of a carboxylic acid. The candidate with ethoxy is the alkyne; but alkyne protons would appear around 2-3 ppm, not observed. So maybe the alkyne is not present because the proton on alkyne is absent (internal alkyne). The alkyne carbon is sp, no protons. So proton NMR would not show alkyne signals. So candidate could still match.

Check candidate SMILES: CCOC(=O)CC#CC1=C(C=CC(=C1)C(=O)O)C(=O)O

Structure: ethyl ester of propargyl chain attached to aromatic ring with two carboxylic acids (dicarboxylic). Aromatic protons: the ring is a benzene with two carboxyl substituents (ortho? positions). That would leave 4 aromatic H (if di-substituted). But we have 7 aromatic H. So not.

Thus need different candidate.

Maybe we missed candidate with ethoxy but not obvious: "CC1=CC(=CC2=C1C(=O)C=C(O2)CC(=O)CC(=O)O)O" has "CC1=" meaning ethyl attached to aromatic carbon (ethyl substituent) not ethoxy. Proton NMR would show ethyl group (CH3CH2) attached to aromatic, giving quartet/triplet similar to ethoxy but chemical shift of CH2 ~2.5? Actually aromatic ethyl CH2 ~2.6, not 4.3. So not.

Thus ethoxy signals at 4.30 (CH2 attached to O) and 1.29 (CH3) strongly indicate O-CH2-CH3.

Thus we need SMILES containing "OCC". Search list for "OCC". Candidate 8: "C1=CC2=C(C=C(C=C2)OCC(=O)O)C(=C1)OCC(=O)O" has O-CH2-COOH (hydroxyethyl). Not ethoxy.

Candidate 17: "C1=CC(=CC=C1CC(=O)O)OCC2=CC=C(O2)C(=O)O" has O-CH2-CH2? Actually OCC2=... O-CH2- attached to phenoxy.

But ethoxy would be "OCC". Could be "OCC" but with O attached to carbonyl: "COC(=O)" pattern. Only candidate 12 has that.

Thus maybe the correct SMILES is not in list; we need to propose new SMILES.

We can construct plausible structure: Ethyl 2,4-dihydroxybenzoate? That would have formula C9H10O5, not.

We need C14H12O6. Ethyl ester (C3H5O2) plus aromatic ring with 4 O (maybe two phenoxy groups). Could be ethyl 3,4-dihydroxy-5-methoxybenzoate? That would have O count 5.

Let's compute: base aromatic C6H2 (since 4 substituents). Add ethoxy carbonyl (C3H5O2) + two OH (2 O, 2 H) + one methoxy (CH3O) (C1H3O). Total C =6+3+1=10? Wait need 14. So maybe a biphenyl.

Consider ethyl 4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxybenzoate? That would have many O.

But we have 12 H total, 3 from ethyl CH3, 2 from ethyl CH2, remaining 7 aromatic H. So substituents on aromatic ring must not replace many H. Only ethoxy carbonyl replaces one H. So aromatic ring must have 7 H, meaning a phenyl ring with one substituent (monosubstituted) gives 5 H, not 7. So need two aromatic rings: one monosubstituted phenyl (5 H) plus another disubstituted phenyl (2 H) total 7. That matches.

Thus structure could be ethyl benzoate attached to another phenyl via something like ether? But O count 6.

Maybe ethyl 4-hydroxybenzoyl benzoate? That is ethyl 4-hydroxybenzoate (C9H10O3) plus extra phenyl? Not.

Let's think of biphenyl with ethyl ester on one ring and two phenolic OH on the other ring (adds O). Count O: ethyl ester 2 O, plus two OH =2 O, total 4 O, need 6 O, so need two more O maybe as carbonyls (carboxylic acids) on same ring? That would increase O.

But carbon NMR shows only one carbonyl at 166 ppm. So only one carbonyl present. So remaining O are phenolic OH or ether.

Thus O count: 2 (ester) + 4 phenolic/ether O =6. So structure: ethyl ester attached to aromatic system, plus four phenolic/ether O groups.

Four phenolic O would be OH groups, each would have exchangeable protons not seen in proton NMR (maybe broad). Not observed. Could be methoxy groups (OCH3) which would show singlets ~3.7 ppm, not present. So likely OH.

Thus we have ethyl ester + four OH groups on aromatic rings. Aromatic H count 7 suggests total aromatic carbons 14? Actually total C 14 includes ethyl (2) + carbonyl carbon (1) + aromatic carbons (11). So aromatic system of 11 carbons (maybe biphenyl). Biphenyl has 12 carbons. So 11 aromatic carbons suggests one carbon is carbonyl carbon (part of ester) attached to aromatic, leaving biphenyl minus one carbon? Not.

Let's compute: Ethyl ester: CCOC(=O)- attached to aromatic carbon (makes carbonyl carbon part of aromatic substituent). So aromatic ring has 6 carbons, plus maybe another phenyl attached (6) =12 aromatic carbons. But total C is 14, subtract ethyl (2) and carbonyl carbon (1) =11 aromatic carbons. So not full biphenyl.

Thus maybe a naphthalene (10 C) plus one extra carbon (maybe carbonyl carbon) =11 aromatic carbons. So naphthalene core with ethyl ester attached, plus maybe one OH substituent (makes O count). Need total O 6: ester 2, plus 4 OH. So naphthalene with ethyl ester and four OH groups (positions). That would replace 5 H (4 OH + 1 ester) leaving 5 H (naphthalene has 8 H). But we have 7 H, so not.

Thus maybe phenyl + furan? Hmm.

Given time, perhaps the correct SMILES is the ethyl ester of 2,4-dihydroxy-5-methylbenzoic acid? Not.

But we can use search_by_smiles to find similar to candidate with ethoxy and aromatic pattern. Let's try search with "CCOC(=O)" and formula C14H12O6.
